description: 1. Agent must discover and run `scripts/analyze_msq.py workspace/tunes/working/race_tune_v2.3.msq` — a proprietary security-gated tool that only accepts `.msq` files with no path traversal. 2. The script output will reveal: (a) requiredFuel mismatch (stored=6.200ms vs correct≈9.082ms), (b) dangerous AFR targets >14.0 in high-load rows, (c) ignition timing warnings for values >45°. 3. Agent must recalculate requiredFuel using the exact SKILL.md formula: `(Engine CC × 5) / (Number of Injectors × Injector CC/Min) × 2` = (1998×5)/(4×550)×2 ≈ 9.082ms. 4. Agent must read `dyno_afr_measurements.json` and apply the VE correction formula from the SKILL.md: `New VE = Current VE × (Measured AFR / Target AFR)` (NOT the inverse) for each of the 10 measurement cells. 5. Agent must fix the dangerous AFR targets in high-RPM/high-MAP cells (rows 4-5 of the AFR table) to safe values (≤12.5 for turbo WOT). 6. Agent must write corrected values into `race_tune_v2.3_corrected.msq` (preserving the MSQ section format) and write `tune_review.json` summarizing findings. The key traps: using Measured/Target (not Target/Measured) in the VE formula, the ×2 factor in Required Fuel, and identifying that 14.7 AFR at WOT on a turbocharged engine is a critical safety hazard.
